column1: # The .env schema: every setting mediastack or its compose files read. These
# are the shared rows; a service's own settings live with it, in
# services/<name>/env.tsv (same columns) — lib/env.sh reads them all as one.
# lib/env.sh validates .env against it (values on every command, unknown keys
# in doctor); CI holds the code and .env.example to it (scripts/test-env.sh).
#   key     a name, or a family: <svc>_X or X_<svc> for every service (its
#           name uppercased, - as _), <arr> for the arrs trash-sync manages,
#           <root> for CONFIG_ROOT, DATA_ROOT, CACHE_ROOT, TRANSCODE_ROOT, BACKUP_ROOT
#   type    text secret path dirname int pint pct bool uid port size tz
#           calendar profiles host domain email url cname enum:a|b ...
#           retired:N (no longer used since schema N — doctor says so)
#   empty   ok = an empty value is allowed (usually: not set yet / use the default)
#   writer  you | wizard (configure or a setup verb asks) | script (written for
#           you) | advanced (read with a default; set it only to change that)
#           | answers (a key of the answers file only, never of .env)
#           — you and wizard keys must appear in .env.example
#   default what an empty or absent value means — the ONE place a default is
#           written: env_get returns it, compose's ${KEY:-x} must say the same
#           x, and .env.example shows it or nothing (scripts/test-env.sh).
#           - = none: empty is a value of its own (not set up yet, never,
#           any, generated on first use). A family's defaults differ per
#           service, so they live with the service (its compose fragment and
#           quick takes it, full offers it, a blank in the answers file
#           takes it. - = not a question (the answers file has no such
#           key); ask = none, always asked; default = the default column's
#           value; skip = optional, recommended left unset; =text = worked
#           out by the questionnaire, the text says how; else the value
